q: The closed graph theorem states that a linear map T: X → Y between Banach spaces is bounded (continuous) if and only if:
opts: The graph {(x,Tx)} is closed in X×Y
exp: Closed graph theorem (consequence of the open mapping theorem): if X, Y are Banach spaces and T is linear with closed graph, then T is continuous. This is frequently used to prove that a naturally defined linear operator is bounded.
